maya: Quick RFC follow-up — I'm proposing we deprecate the 'prefix-ownership-v1' explicit-transfer API and adopt a soft-credit reclamation model for prefix cache residency.

maya: TL;DR: instead of explicit handoff tokens + strict fencing, nodes earn/lose soft credits for a prefix based on recent traffic and can voluntarily demote when credits drop below a threshold. This reduces cross-node consensus and should improve churn under bursty multi-tenant workloads.

maya: sketch of semantics:
```
- each prefix has an epoch (monotonic counter) and a soft-credit integer per node.
- on access, node increments its local credit for that prefix (capped).
- background evaporator decays credit over time.
- eviction decision: global coordinator compares credits (approx) and asks high-credit nodes to keep; low-credit nodes demote proactively.
- critical: epoch ties break by epoch+node-id to avoid split-brain.
```

trent: This sounds promising. Main Q: how do we maintain correctness for in-flight writes/long-lived cursors? Ownership API protected those with fences.

maya: Good call. Plan is to keep a tiny strict lease for write-affecting operations only (10s TTL) — read-heavy prefixes follow soft-credits. So we don't regress R/W correctness; we only relax read residency.

arjun: Concern: coordinator still needs a view of credits. If it's eventually consistent we might ask a node to demote while it has active KV-cache in use. How do we avoid racey demote evict causing tail latencies?

maya: Mitigation ideas:
- demote request returns a grace token allowing inflight readers Nms to finish.
- demote is a stepped operation: soft-demote -> mark-compact -> evict. Each step is observed via lightweight per-prefix counters. If counters spike, demote aborts.

sasha: Can we piggyback credit heartbeats on existing telemetry to avoid extra control-plane chatter? e.g., embed credit delta in the per-request trace header.

maya: Yes. Credit deltas are tiny ints; we can fold them into existing metrics blobs. Coordinator only requires periodic summaries, not every access.

trent: What about cold-start and fairness? A node serving many cold prefixes could get poisoned by initial low credit.

maya: We'll bootstrap new prefixes with a bias credit (short warmup window). Fairness also handled by tenant-weighted credit allocation — bigger paid tenants get higher cap.

arjun: Implementation complexity: we currently have eviction pipeline tied to slab-allocator internals. Soft-credit demote needs a thin adapter there. I can prototype an adapter that maps demote stages -> slab compaction hints.

sasha: Operational tooling: need new dashboard rows: per-prefix credit, demote-rate, demote-aborts. Also an alert when demote-aborts > X in 5m.

evict-bot: [automated] note: running simulated chaos tests with 50k prefixes and bursty traffic shows 23% lower cross-node handoff ops and similar p99 read latency.

maya: Tradeoffs summary (short):
- Pros: fewer cross-node RPCs, better throughput under churn, simpler long-term dir structure.
- Cons: added heuristic tuning (decay rate, caps), edge cases for long-lived writers require small strict leases.

maya: Decision proposal: move forward with a 3-week spike: 1) prototype adapter for slab demote (arjun), 2) telemetry + coordinator proto (sasha), 3) correctness tests for writer lease interactions (trent).

trent: ack, will own writer-lease correctness tests. I'll mock long-lived cursor scenarios and failure injection.

arjun: I'll start the prototype branch and try to keep adapter surface minimal.

sasha: I'll add credit telemetry to the per-request beacon and a quick Grafana panel.

maya: Cool. Follow-ups: PRs in two weeks, integration test run in week 3. @evict-bot schedule chaos sim after week 3. :thumbsup:

trent: :+1:

arjun: :rocket:

sasha: :eyes:
